_comment: Curated product-domain acceptance-criteria sets for Story 6.3's evaluation.
PROVENANCE — read before using these numbers. These are 'agent_authored':
written by the dev agent for this evaluation. They are NOT human-authored,
and they are NOT real Jira tickets. What they are is ON-DOMAIN: they
describe product behaviour of the kind this application converts from Jira
tickets, which the Story 6.5 training corpus almost entirely lacked (84% of
it was testing-framework Gherkin about running CLI commands).
They carry NO reference Gherkin, so reference-similarity scoring does not
apply to them — only the structural metrics and the blinded judge. Report
them as their own group; do not average them with the holdout.
Replace these with real Jira tickets as soon as the app has been used on
20+. That would upgrade provenance from agent_authored to human_jira and is
the single biggest available improvement to this evaluation's validity.

items.acceptance_criteria:
AC1: A registered user can request a password reset link by submitting their email address.
AC2: A reset link expires one hour after it is issued, and using an expired link shows an explanatory message rather than a generic error.
AC3: Requesting a reset for an email address that is not registered returns the same confirmation as a registered one, so the response does not reveal whether an account exists.

AC1: A user who enters an incorrect password five times in a row within fifteen minutes is locked out for thirty minutes.
AC2: A successful login resets the failed-attempt counter to zero.
AC3: A locked-out user attempting to log in is told when the lockout expires.

AC1: A customer can pay for an order with a saved card without re-entering the card number.
AC2: If the payment provider declines the card, the order remains unpaid and the customer sees the decline reason.
AC3: A payment that succeeds at the provider but times out before confirmation is reconciled automatically and is never charged twice.

AC1: A customer can request a full refund within thirty days of purchase.
AC2: A refund request after thirty days is rejected with the purchase date shown.
AC3: A partially refunded order cannot be refunded again beyond its remaining balance.

AC1: A user can filter search results by category and by price range simultaneously.
AC2: Clearing all filters restores the unfiltered result set without losing the search term.
AC3: A filter combination that matches nothing shows an empty state suggesting which filter to relax.

AC1: A user can upload a PDF or DOCX file up to 10 MB to a project.
AC2: A file exceeding 10 MB is rejected before upload begins, with the limit stated.
AC3: An unsupported file type is rejected and the list of supported types is shown.
AC4: An upload interrupted by a lost connection can be retried without creating a duplicate.

AC1: A workspace administrator can change another member's role between viewer, editor and administrator.
AC2: An administrator cannot remove their own administrator role if they are the only administrator left.
AC3: A viewer who attempts to edit a document is shown a read-only notice instead of an editor.

AC1: A user can turn email notifications on or off per notification type.
AC2: Turning off all notification types stops all emails except security alerts, which cannot be disabled.
AC3: A preference change takes effect for notifications generated after the change, not retroactively.

AC1: A user can book a meeting room for a time slot that is currently free.
AC2: Booking a slot that overlaps an existing booking is refused and the conflicting booking's time is shown.
AC3: Two users submitting a booking for the same free slot at the same moment result in exactly one booking, and the loser is told the slot was taken.

AC1: An API client may make up to 100 requests per minute per API key.
AC2: A request beyond the limit is rejected with HTTP 429 and a header stating when the limit resets.
AC3: Rate-limit counters are tracked per API key, so one client exhausting its quota does not affect another.
